questions.question:
Given below is a statement Followed by two conclusions I and II. Study the statement carefully and decide which Conclusion/s is/are definitely true.

Statement: M ≥ N > O ≥ P = W; X ≥ O > Y

Conclusion I: M > X

Conclusion II: W < Y

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II is true.
Both Conclusions I and II are true.

questions.solution:
Given statement: M ≥ N > O ≥ P = W; X ≥ O > Y

Conclusions:

Conclusion I : M > X → False (As __**M**__ ≥ N > O ≤ __X__. So, no relation between M and X can be determined therefore it is definitely false.)

Conclusion II : W False (As __**W**__ = N ≤ O > __Y__. So, no relation between W and Y can be determined therefore it is definitely false.)

Thus, Neither Conclusion I nor II is true.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

18 : 325

__**18²**__ + 1 = 325

__**324 + 1**__ = 325

325 = 325 (LHS = RHS)

And,

12 : 145

__144 + 1__ = 145

145 = 145 (LHS = RHS)

__82__ + 1 = 63

__64 + 1__ = 63

65 ≠ 63 (LHS ≠ RHS)

__162__ + 1 = 257

__256 + 1__ = 257

**257 = 257 (LHS = RHS)**

Option 3) 15 : 225 

__152__ + 1 = 225

__225 + 1__ = 225

226 ≠ 225 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Option 4) 9 : 81

__92__ + 1 = 81

__81 + 1__ = 81

82 ≠ 81 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '16 : 257' follows the same logic as given.

Hence, **"Option 2"** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. 

**Statements:**

No letter is an alphabet

All alphabets are words.

**Conclusions:**

I. All words can never be letters.

II. All letters being words is a possibility.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e27c1e8652aa4548ec4458c41690de3b3fab0d28aa24d15cbe2798edc06d903.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All words can never be letters → Follow (As no letter is an alphabet and all alphabets are words. As all letters cannot be alphabets which whole comes in words, therefore it is true)

II. All letters being words is a possibility → Follow (As no letter is an alphabet and all alphabets are words. As no statement restricts whole letters from being words, therefore it is possible)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II follow.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2"

questions.question: Suresh is now 19 years old and in college. Since he was a 5-year-old, he stayed in a hostel and is now coming back home after 14 long years. His parents have texted him the direction from the railway station to his house. See the below text message sent to Suresh by his parents and answer the following question accordingly. "When you step out of the railway station, you are facing north. Take a right and drive 4 km, you will see a T-point/junction. Take a right and drive 2 km. There will be a roundabout with four roads. Take the second left from the round-about and drive 1 km. Take a right and drive 3 km. Take a left and drive 2 km. You will find our house at the front. Come home fast.". How many kilometres did Suresh drive to reach his home from the railway station?
questions.solution:
Given:

When you step out of the railway station, you are facing north.

Take a right and drive 4 km, you will see a T-point/junction.

Take a right and drive 2 km.

There will be a roundabout with four roads.

Take the second left from the round-about and drive 1 km.

Take a right and drive 3 km. Take a left and drive 2 km. You will find our house at the front.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dec00f48fbbe799f9987d3da0fdd6797e4dd5f38d5668450570775f8be42cdf0.png] 

Thus, Suresh drove (4 km + 2 km + 1 km + 3 km + 2 km) 12 km to reach his home from the railway station.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. 

**Statements:**

All dahlias are lilies.

All sunflowers are lilies.

Some dahlias are hibiscus.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some sunflowers are not dahlias.

II. Some hibiscuses are not lilies.

III. Some lilies are hibiscus.

options.text: Both conclusion II and III follow.
Both conclusion I and III follow.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef56002e0d757b60fc13bcdb7d1366b52dcda64d077fed7fcba4467edf4c3421.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some sunflowers are not dahlias → Does not follow (As all dahlias are lilies and all sunflowers are lilies. As no direct relation is given dahlias and sunflowers, therefore it is false)

II. Some hibiscuses are not lilies → Does not follow (As all dahlias are lilies and some dahlias are hibiscus. As no direct relation is given hibiscus and lilies, therefore it is false)

III. Some lilies are hibiscus → Follow (As all dahlias are lilies and some dahlias are hibiscus. As some part of hibiscus is common with dahlias which whole comes in lilies, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion III follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1"

questions.question: K, L, M, W, X, Y and Z scored different marks in an exam. K scored more than both L and W but less than Y. X scored less than only Y. Neither L nor M scored the lowest marks. Z scored more than L, but less than M. K scored more than M. Who scored the third-lowest marks?
questions.solution:
**Given: **K, L, M, W, X, Y and Z scored different marks in an exam.

1) X scored less than only Y.

Y > X > _ > _ > _ > _ > _

2) K scored more than both L and W but less than Y.

3) K scored more than M.

4) Neither L nor M scored the lowest marks.

Case 1) Y > X > K > L/W/M > L/W/M > L/W/M > _

Case 2) Y > X > K > _ > L/M > L/M > W

Case 3) Y > X > K > L/M > _ > L/M > W

Case 4) Y > X > _ > K > L/M > L/M > W

5) Z scored more than L, but less than M.

As, there is no possible position for Z in case 1, 2 and 4, therefore are eliminated.

Case 3) Y > X > K > M > Z > L > W

Thus, according to the final arrangement Z scored the third-lowest marks.

Hence, **"Option 1"** is the correct answer.
